patterns_observed: 5 posts lack EPISTEMIC FLAGS sections — articles 6, 7, 8, 9, and llm-factors-psychology. All other ICESCR article posts include them. Structural inconsistency across the series.
4 posts lack CC BY-SA footer — same posts minus article 9. Not included in top 10 but noted as a co-occurring structural gap.

Body-text confidence often exceeds epistemic-flag hedging — posts that include epistemic flags sections honestly acknowledge uncertainty, but the body text presents the same claims without hedging. A careful reader would notice this gap.
E-Prime discipline holds well across most posts. Article 3 achieves zero violations. Article 6 carries 7 violations — the heaviest debt in the scan.
Vocabulary consistency holds excellently. ICESCR, CESCR, progressive realization, non-retrogression, ratification, states parties all appear correctly throughout.

epistemic_flags: Scan performed by 3 parallel sub-agents; findings consolidated by the parent agent. Sub-agent line-number accuracy depends on file state at scan time — verify line numbers against HEAD.
E-Prime violations in quoted treaty text receive a pass by design; some borderline cases (e.g., 'has' constructions) may reflect judgment calls.
Fair-witness findings identify missing citations but do not verify whether cited sources exist or support the claims made.
